title: Loch Ness witness spots 'seven-metre' creature moving 'like a very large eel'
excerpt: The Official Loch Ness Monster Sightings Register has added two new reports to its 2026 list, after tourists from Malta and Spain claimed to have spotted a mysterious creature in the Scottish Highlands loch
content:
The Official Loch Ness Monster Sightings Register has added two new reports to its 2026 list, after tourists from Malta and Spain claimed to have spotted a mysterious creature in the Scottish Highlands loch

For generations, the legend of the Loch Ness Monster has captivated imaginations, with countless people becoming fascinated by tales of the enigmatic creature said to lurk beneath the waters of Loch Ness in northern Scotland.

The loch, located just under a four-hour drive from Glasgow, has long been a place of intrigue and mystique, particularly due to the alleged serpentine creature some believe inhabits its depths, a legend that has endured for nearly a century.

Fresh claims have emerged of further sightings of the Loch Ness Monster, often known as 'Nessie', with the Official Loch Ness Monster Sightings Register recording new reports for 2026, bringing the year's total to 15.

The accounts came from holidaymakers visiting the UK from Malta and Spain on 5 and 6 August. The first sighting was reported by Norbert Kawka, who claimed to have witnessed the Loch Ness Monster at 20:50 on 5 August during an encounter that reportedly lasted approximately 15 minutes.

Regarding this encounter, a spokesperson for the Official Sightings Register stated that Mr Kawka "saw a creature move against the current, in and out of the water like a very large eel".

They continued: "The weather was foggy with a hint of rain, there was no wind and water conditions were calm. He estimated that the size was at least seven metres in length."

However, Mr Kawka's encounter would not be the last, as just hours later, Jocelyn Boyce, who had travelled to Scotland from Barcelona, Spain, claimed she had witnessed something in the loch while exploring the famous location, reports the Daily Star.

Describing her experience, Jocelyn explained that she was accompanied by her family when they observed "a dark, almost black, mound-like shape protruding above the surface of the water".
